record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: For any triangle T in the Euclidean plane, does there exist a 3-coloring of all points of the plane such that no congruent copy of T has all three vertices the same color?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. For any triangle T , there exists a 3-coloring of E2 without a monochromatic copy of T .

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $T$ be a triangle in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ (that is, an unordered set of three non-collinear points). A coloring $\chi : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \{1,2,3\}$ is said to contain a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$ if there exist three points $p_1, p_2, p_3 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ forming a triangle congruent to $T$ with $\chi(p_1)=\chi(p_2)=\chi(p_3)$. Prove or disprove the following statement: for every triangle $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, there exists a 3-coloring $\chi : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \{1,2,3\}$ that contains no monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that for every triangle T there is a 3-coloring of the plane avoiding monochromatic congruent copies of T is a well-known open problem in Euclidean Ramsey theory. Progress has focused mainly on the dual 2-coloring conjecture (where recent 2024 work confirmed it for 3-term arithmetic progressions), but the general 3-coloring statement for arbitrary triangles remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Biggest Open Problem in Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Patel, UChicago REU)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems in Euclidean Ramsey theory, including triangle coloring conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Triangle avoidance coloring conjectures are presented as open problems in Euclidean Ramsey theory.

status_evidence.title: Any two-coloring of the plane contains monochromatic 3-term arithmetic progressions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent progress on a related Erdős–Graham–Montgomery–Rothschild–Spencer–Straus conjecture; the general triangle case remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Related two-coloring conjecture is open in general; only special cases (e.g., 3-APs) have been settled, suggesting the 3-coloring version for general triangles is also open.

status_evidence.title: TOPP Problem 58: Monochromatic Triangles
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem entry on monochromatic triangle Ramsey-type questions in the plane.
